history.content: what is the difference between monte carlo and monaco

Monte Carlo, one of Europe's leading tourist resorts, is actually a part of Monaco, which is a sovereign city-state located on the French Riviera. Specifically, Monte Carlo refers to an administrative area or ward within Monaco, and is known for the Monte Carlo Casino. It's also used informally to refer to a larger district, the Monte Carlo Quarter, which includes several other wards. On the other hand, Monaco is a country, and it consists of four traditional quarters: Fontvieille, Monaco-Ville, La Condamine, and Monte Carlo. It too is a key tourist destination, with many tourist attractions all centered in Monaco-Ville. While Monte Carlo is a part of Monaco, the term "Monaco" is often used to refer to the country as a whole.
what movies were filmed in Monte Carlo?

The Monte Carlo Casino was featured in the James Bond films Never Say Never Again ( 1983 ) , and GoldenEye ( 1995 ). To Catch a Thief ( 1954 ) was an Alfred Hitchcock film with Monte Carlo's casino as the setting and featured Cary Grant and Grace Kelly , the future Princess Grace of Monaco , as the stars . There is a scene in the movie where the-then Grace Kelly drives a car very quickly -- and dangerously -- along the steep winding roads of Monaco that surround the heights of Monte Carlo ; an interesting coincidence to her actual fate in 1982 . Monte Carlo also served as a location for a 1960s British series -- Randall and Hopkirk ( Deceased )  --  episode, again taking place in the casino. Grand Prix (1966) and Herbie Goes to Monte Carlo (1977) were also filmed there.  And the motor race Monaco World Prix 1 in Monte Carlo also featured in the 2010 film Iron Man 2 . Monte Carlo was also the setting for several other films, and has been featured as a location in some video games as well as animations.
It is so eerie that Princess Grace's death was foreshadowed in To Catch a Thief.

Yes, it is quite an eerie coincidence that the scene in To Catch a Thief shows Grace Kelly driving recklessly along the winding roads of Monaco, which is reminiscent of her actual fate in 1982 when she died in a car accident in the same area.
Were any safety improvements made to the roads in Monaco after her death?
